record.context_brief: Physical meaning of Jordan and Einstein frames
record.original_question: When modified gravitational dynamics are written in the Jordan frame, where Einstein field equations are modified and matter fields are minimally coupled to gravity, or in the Einstein frame, where Einstein field equations are preserved and matter fields are non-minimally coupled, does passing from one conformal frame to the other have genuine physical significance?

evidence.quote: In the case where Einstein field equations are modified and matter field are minimally coupled with gravity, we are dealing with the so-called Jordan frame. In the case where Einstein field equations are preserved and matter field are non-minimally coupled, we are dealing with the so-called Einstein frame.
Both frames are conformally related but the very final issue is to understand if passing from one frame to the other (and vice versa) is physically significant.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a scalar–tensor theory of gravity formulated on a 4-dimensional spacetime manifold with Lorentzian metric g and a scalar field φ. Two equivalent mathematical descriptions of such theories are commonly used:

(1) The Jordan frame: the metric g_J satisfies modified Einstein field equations (with φ entering non-trivially as a multiplicative factor of the Ricci scalar in the gravitational action), while matter fields ψ_m are minimally coupled to g_J, so that test particles follow geodesics of g_J.

(2) The Einstein frame: after a conformal transformation g_E = Ω(φ)^2 g_J (with Ω a strictly positive smooth function of φ), together with a corresponding redefinition of the scalar field, the gravitational action takes the standard Einstein–Hilbert form, but matter fields couple non-minimally to g_E through Ω(φ).

The two descriptions are related by a conformal rescaling of the metric and field redefinitions, and are mathematically equivalent at the level of the classical action.

Question: Determine whether the passage from the Jordan frame to the Einstein frame (and back) carries genuine physical significance — that is, whether the two frames describe the same physical theory, or whether observable predictions (for example involving matter trajectories, energy conditions, singularity structure, or quantum effects such as entanglement and vacuum states) can in principle distinguish them. Provide a precise criterion under which the two frames are physically equivalent, and conditions under which they are not.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether Jordan and Einstein frames are physically equivalent remains actively debated. At the classical level, recent work (e.g., 2024 results in Eur. Phys. J. C) supports a canonical/Hamiltonian equivalence on a reduced phase space, and many authors argue equivalence since conformal rescalings cannot be measured absolutely. At the quantum level, however, multiple recent studies (2023–2025) show inequivalence: loop quantization, entanglement-based probes, and inflationary magnetogenesis distinguish the frames. The physical equivalence is therefore considered open, with partial classical results but unresolved quantum-level status.

status_evidence.title: Jordan and Einstein frames - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Their physical equivalence has been debated, with various arguments on both sides.
status_evidence.claim: The physical equivalence between the two frames remains debated.

status_evidence.title: On the canonical equivalence between Jordan and Einstein frames
status_evidence.snippet: Transformations from the Jordan to the Einstein frame are Hamiltonian canonical on the reduced phase space.
status_evidence.claim: Classical canonical equivalence has been established under gauge fixing (partial result).

status_evidence.title: Distinguishing Jordan and Einstein frames in gravity through entanglement
status_evidence.snippet: At the quantum level the two frames exhibit subtle differences that entanglement between massive objects can probe.
status_evidence.claim: Quantum-level inequivalence is suggested by entanglement probes, indicating the question is still open.

status_evidence.title: Equivalence of the Einstein and Jordan frames
status_evidence.snippet: Argues classical equivalence of Einstein and Jordan frames.
status_evidence.claim: Classical equivalence has been argued in the literature.
